title: Father's move to Tuskegee and his Wesleyan education
summary: His father takes a job at Tuskegee under Booker T. Washington; Wilson describes his father's Wesleyan degree, the yearbook gift, and $163 college tuition.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And then my father got a better job at Tuskegee Institute under Booker T. Washington -- and I guess that
would have been maybe around 1915 or '16, something like that, and then the whole family had moved to Alabama.*
Yeah, Tuskegee, the Tuskegee Institute, and the third part of Tuskegee was a big VA hospital, but that came later after the first world war.

Tell me this, Teddy -- it's quite unusual, I mean, I'm from the south, and your parents were both professors in education. They were much ahead of their time for that era, of black people having this kind of an educational background, isn't that right?

That is true. My father was. My mother, at that time, when I was born, she had a high school education. She had gone to what we called State Normal or the other name for it was Alabama State in Montgomery, Alabama.

But my father had come south from the north. He had graduated with honors from Wesleyan University in Middletown, Connecticut, in the graduating class of 1907, and incidentally, I have -- as a very nice gift, it was given to me a few years ago; I was playing at the Sheraton Tobacco Valley Inn on Route 91, just north of Hartford, and some of the students from Wesleyan made me

a surprise present of xerox pages from the yearbook of 1907 with my father's picture in it, and his whole -- you know, the paragraphs they put in there, the honors he won that year, and who gave him his degree and so on, like that.

So that's a very prize possession I have. If these students hadn't made me a surprise gift of that, I would never have had, you know, except hearsay from my relatives, that my father went to that school. But I do actually have photostat pictures of him and two of his classmates on the same page.

Incidentally, before I go any further, the interesting side light, is that in those days, I remember clearly -- the tuition and the room and board for one man -- two in a room -- but one man, was only $163 a year. That's in a college, now.
That was for a college education, room and board, and two men in a room -- $163. That's a long time passed, isn't it?

I'm telling you; that's amazing. It's interesting to hear that. And that's just so good, Teddy. Now about your parents -- before I interject this, you were in Tuskegee and your parents had gotten to Tuskegee. Now go on from there.
